definition: A 1.5B Qwen2.5 model, used across 3 sources as a small subject for test-time refinement, token-selection training and trajectory-geometry evaluation. Its measured appearances: a sparsity ablation on it finds a 10 percent unique-token selection giving 66.23 pass@1 against 63.37 at 20 percent, 60.62 for the bottom 90 percent of frequent tokens and 57.45 for the standard baseline -- one of the archive's cleaner demonstrations that which tokens are trained on matters more than how many. It also appears in an entropy-informed selection study reaching 66.2 percent majority-vote accuracy against a 60.8 baseline.

evidence.note: Spends test-time compute on iteratively refining each sampled rollout rather than on drawing more of them, then majority-votes the refined answers, with no verifier.
evidence.title: Refining Over Resampling: Test-Time Self-Correction for LLM Reasoning

evidence.note: Argues that Shannon entropy is the wrong criterion for picking which tokens to train on in RLVR, and selects tokens instead by the Jensen-Shannon divergence of their logit distribution from the group average, updating only the top 10% of these 'unique' tokens.
evidence.title: Beyond Entropy: Learning from Token-Level Distributional Deviations for LLM Reasoning

evidence.note: TRACED scores a reasoning chain by the geometry of its hidden-state trajectory -- net displacement as progress and curvature as stability -- and uses the two as features for a Gaussian classifier that separates correct from incorrect chains without reading the text.
evidence.title: Beyond Scalars: Evaluating and Understanding LLM Reasoning via Geometric Progress and Stability

name: Qwen2.5-1.5B
